thread:
sara.k: seeing a steady throughput drop in gpu-rt-us-west-2 pool, 99th latency spiking and a bunch of job evictions. suspecting PCIe/NVLink/backpressure.
mike.l: which nodes? logs?

sara.k: nodes affected: node-51-12, node-51-13, node-51-14. dmesg shows repeated AER and Xid messages. sample:
```
[ 1234.567890] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: id=0000
[ 1234.567891] nvidia 0000:66:00.0: Xid (31) 00000000 GPU fault: Default engine
[ 1234.567892] nvlink: link 3 lost sync, retrying
[ 1234.567895] pcie 0000:65:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer
```
sara.k: spike correlates with NVLink retransmits and stalled kernels, queue_depth climbs, scheduler starts evicting long jobs.

jordan.t: driver/kernel versions same across the rack? any recent BIOS or PCIe firmware changes pushed to rack51?

sara.k: we rolled the 470->525 driver last week on rack51 as part of throughput testing. BIOS stayed the same.

nina.p: high-level mitigation options:
- quickly reduce cross-card NVLink traffic (so affected card doesn't stall peer) by routing heavy shard placement off those nodes
- set `pci=noaer` temporarily to stop log storms while we triage (reduces noise but hides correctable AERs)
- drain the two most-faulty nodes and run targeted stress + `nvidia-bug-report.sh`

mike.l: inventory check: we have 2 spare A100-HX in us-west-2 pool. RMA queue is 3 days for replacements shipped from staging region.

sara.k: I'm proposing immediate actions:
1) `redwoodctl node drain node-51-12 --reason "AER/NVLink flaps"` (manual canary)
2) run `ssh node-51-12 -- sudo ./nvidia-bug-report.sh` and upload to s3://redwood-dumps/bugreports/2005341123/
3) if consistent Xid31 on same GPU, cordon node and schedule on-site swap using spare if available
4) if not, try BIOS/PCIe link retrain and re-run workload

infra-bot: automated threshold hit: node-51-12 AER_count > 100 within 1h, triggering recommended drain. https://console.redwood/ops/alerts/2005341123

mike.l: +1 to drain. I'll reserve a spare and book a 4h maintenance window with oncall. ETA to replace if approved: 4h (on-site swap) + 1h validation.

jordan.t: a note on root cause hunting: AER + NVLink flaps together often point at signal integrity or power sequencing issues on the riser/card. If we see bursts timed with VM live-migration or rack power re-probes, correlate with PDUs. Also check PCIe AER counters per slot via `setpci` and measure lane training failures.

nina.p: short-term routing change: recommend we add a routing policy to avoid the us-west-2-gpu pool for high-p99 sensitive routes until we confirm stable. `redwoodctl route update --avoid-pool gpu-rt-us-west-2 --until 2005346720` (tactical)

sara.k: approved. I'll kick the drain for node-51-12 now and start bugreport. tagging @mike.l for spare swap coordination.

mike.l: I'll handle the swap. will post status updates in this thread. :wrench: 

sara.k: thanks — after swap, we'll run the standard validation: 30m of stress workloads + p99 latency check + nvlink stress test. if green, rejoin pool.

jordan.t: if replacement doesn't clear flaps, escalate to hardware vendor for cable/riser RMA. may need to repro in lab with same driver/BIOS combo.

sara.k: noted. logging action items to infra-runbook -> incidents -> 2005341123. will post the bugreport link when ready.

mike.l: started maintenance ticket #INF-4592. ETA swap start: 2026-03-22T15:30Z

sara.k: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. keeping thread open for updates.
